**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 18 of the MSA already contains a vendor-side insurance covenant that meets or exceeds our preferred position:

| Playbook requirement | Section 18.1 |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M/occurrence, 2M aggregate | ✅ Matches exactly |
| Professional (E&O) USD 2M | ✅ Matches |
| Cyber/privacy USD 5M (vendor processes Customer Data) | ✅ Matches |
| Workers' compensation as required by law | ✅ Plus employer's liability USD 1M (extra) |
| Certificates on request | ✅ Section 18.2, plus evidence of coverage |

Supporting points that made this a clean pass rather than a needs-review:

- **Duration** — coverage runs throughout the term *and for one year afterward*, tracking our model language.
- **At Vendor's expense** — no cost pass-through to us.
- **No liability cap leakage** — Section 18.2 states "Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities," so the limits do not undercut the indemnities in Section 20 or the Excluded Claims carve-outs in Section 21.3.
- **Cancellation notice** — Section 18.2 requires advance notice of cancellation or material reduction. It is qualified by "to the extent available from its insurer," which is softer than ideal but is market-standard and not worth a redline given the limits are already at our preferred level.
- **Data sensitivity check** — Vendor processes Customer Data and personal information (Sections 15.1, 15.2, 17.1), which is exactly the trigger for the USD 5M cyber requirement; that limit is present, so we are well clear of the walk-away position.

Direction check: every obligation in Section 18 binds Silverline (Vendor) and benefits Redwood (Customer), so there is nothing here to push back on.
